page: Hono web framework overview. Small, simple, ultrafast framework built on Web Standards. Runs on Cloudflare Workers, Fastly Compute, Deno, Bun, Vercel, AWS Lambda, Lambda@Edge, Node.js via adapter. hono/tiny preset under 14kB; Express 572KB comparison. RegExpRouter (single large Regex, fastest), SmartRouter, LinearRouter, PatternRouter. Built-in middleware: Basic Auth, Bearer Auth, Body Limit, Cache, Compress, Context Storage, Cookie, CORS, ETag, html, JSX, JWT, Logger, Language, Pretty JSON, Secure Headers, SSG, Streaming. Third-party: GraphQL Server, Firebase Auth, Sentry. Context object for Request/Response access. TypeScript support with literal types for path parameters. Validator and hc (Hono Client) enable RPC mode with Zod. Zero dependencies, Web Standards only. Use cases: APIs, proxy, CDN front, edge apps, libraries, full-stack. Benchmarks: Hono 402,820 ops/sec vs itty-router 212,598, sunder 297,036, worktop 197,345. Production users: cdnjs, Cloudflare D1, Cloudflare Workers KV, BaseAI, Unkey, OpenStatus, Deno Benchmarks, Clerk, Drivly, repeat.dev. Questions: What platforms does Hono run on? How small is Hono? What middleware is included? Why is Hono fast? How does TypeScript support work? What license or cost?

sections.manifest: Quick Start installation. Commands for npm, yarn, pnpm, bun, deno: npm create hono@latest, yarn create hono, pnpm create hono@latest, bun create hono@latest, deno init --npm hono@latest. Creates new Hono project.

Hono features: Ultrafast (RegExpRouter, non-linear matching), Lightweight (hono/tiny under 14kB, zero dependencies, Web Standards only), Multi-runtime (Cloudflare Workers, Fastly Compute, Deno, Bun, AWS Lambda, Node.js), Batteries Included (built-in middleware, custom middleware, third-party middleware, helpers), Delightful DX (clean APIs, first-class TypeScript, Types). Questions: How fast is the router? How small is the bundle? Which runtimes are supported? What middleware/helpers are available? Why choose Hono over Express?

Hono use cases: Building Web APIs, proxy of backend servers, front of CDN, edge application, base server for a library, full-stack application. Similar to Express but without frontend. Works on CDN edges. Supports middleware for larger applications. Framework comparison: simpler than full frameworks, more complete than minimal routers. Questions: What can I build with Hono? Can I run it on CDN edges? Can I use it for APIs? What scale applications? Is it suitable for microservices?

Production users of Hono: cdnjs (Cloudflare Workers, free CDN API server), Cloudflare D1 (Cloudflare Workers, serverless SQL databases internal API), Cloudflare Workers KV (Cloudflare Workers, serverless key-value database internal API), BaseAI (Local AI Server, AI agent framework), Unkey (Cloudflare Workers, API authentication/authorization), OpenStatus (Bun, website/API monitoring), Deno Benchmarks (Deno, benchmarking), Clerk (Cloudflare Workers, user management platform), Drivly (Cloudflare Workers), repeat.dev (Cloudflare Workers). See GitHub discussions honojs/discussions/1510 for more. Questions: Who uses Hono in production? What companies trust Hono? Is it used at scale? What types of projects? Can I see examples?

Hono performance benchmarks. Hono 402,820 ops/sec ±4.78% (80 runs), itty-router 212,598 ops/sec ±3.11% (87 runs), sunder 297,036 ops/sec ±4.76% (77 runs), worktop 197,345 ops/sec ±2.40% (88 runs). Fastest is Hono. Benchmarked on Cloudflare Workers routers. Link to full benchmarks at /docs/concepts/benchmarks. Questions: How fast is Hono compared to alternatives? What are the benchmark numbers? Where can I find detailed benchmarks?

Hono size metrics. hono/tiny preset under 14kB minified. Wrangler CLI example output: 11.47 KiB total upload, 4.34 KiB gzip. Middleware and adapters bundled only when used. Express comparison: 572KB. Questions: How small is hono/tiny? What's the gzip size? How does Hono compare to Express in size? Can I see actual bundle outputs? What gets bundled?

Hono router types: RegExpRouter (fastest router in JavaScript, single large Regex created before dispatch, matches routes via pattern), SmartRouter (supports all route patterns with RegExpRouter performance), LinearRouter (registers routes very quickly, suitable for apps that reinitialize), PatternRouter (simple pattern matching, smallest size). Link to /docs/concepts/routers for details. Questions: What routers are available? Which is fastest? When to use each router? How do routers work?

Hono Web Standards platform support. Runs on: Cloudflare Workers, Fastly Compute, Deno, Bun, Vercel, AWS Lambda, Lambda@Edge, Others. Node.js support via honojs/node-server adapter. Platform-agnostic thanks to Web Standards. Link to /docs/concepts/web-standard. Questions: What platforms does Hono support? Does it work on Node.js? How to run on different platforms? Hono middleware and helpers inventory. Built-in: Basic Authentication, Bearer Authentication, Body Limit, Cache, Compress, Context Storage, Cookie, CORS, ETag, html helper, JSX, JWT Authentication, Logger, Language, Pretty JSON, Secure Headers, SSG, Streaming. Third-party packages: GraphQL Server (honojs/middleware/graphql-server), Firebase Authentication (honojs/middleware/firebase-auth), Sentry (honojs/middleware/sentry), Others. Example code: import {etag} from 'hono/etag', import {logger} from 'hono/logger', app.use(etag(), logger()). Questions: What middleware is built-in? What third-party middleware exists? How to add middleware? What helpers are available? Can I write custom middleware?

Hono Developer Experience features. TypeScript support with first-class types. Context object for easy Request/Response access. Path parameters as literal types (example: /entry/:date/:id parameters typed as 'date' | 'id'). Validator support. hc (Hono Client) for RPC mode. Zod validator integration. Type-safe client-server communication. Share server-side API specs with client. Stacks pattern for composition. Link to /docs/concepts/stacks. Questions: Does Hono have TypeScript support? How are path parameters typed? What is RPC mode? Can I use Zod with Hono? How to share types with client?
